title: Ghana: Dangerous Drugs Record
notice: A starting point, not certified for the country. Check each column against the instrument before you rely on it. The Act names the book and what is recorded before a Class A supply, in that order; it sets no layout, no retention period for the book and no way to correct an entry, so this set keeps it 10 years and corrects by a reversing line (the strictest). Every supply out is entered (a sale, an issue, a disposal), not a move between the shop's own stores or a loss; no column is required on the Desk, so a disposal the regulator witnesses is never refused. Until the register door books a return by its direction, a customer's return prints as a supply: mark it by hand. The book is also kept by a Class B supplier (s. 34(1)), but the Act sets no entry for a Class B supply: none is booked here.

books.title: Dangerous Drugs Record
books.cite: Act 489 s. 34(1)-(2): recorded before each Class A supply; s. 34(3) waives the entry where the prescription is retained and referred to (not taken here: every supply is entered)
books.medium_note: A book by name (s. 34(1)); the Act says nothing of electronic records: print each day's pages, sign them and keep them as the book. The Act states no period for this book: 10 years is this set's choice (the prescription itself is kept two years, s. 32(b)).
